findings.explanation: The SPL uses one fixed `poe_w>25` for every port and has no PoE class or allocated-power field, so no class budget comparison happens (implementation vs spl).
findings.suggested_fix: State which PoE budget (allocated or class maximum) is compared and add that field, or describe 25 W as a single global threshold.

findings.explanation: PoE port power comes from the network switch (SNMP power-ethernet MIBs or vendor APIs), not an NVR diagnostic feed; `ifDescr` is an IF-MIB field from the switch.
findings.suggested_fix: Name the switch SNMP source and sourcetype, and which switch MIB exposes per-port power consumption.

findings.explanation: References cover ONVIF and Hikvision only; none documents PoE power telemetry or IEEE 802.3af/at classes.
findings.suggested_fix: Reference the switch vendor's PoE monitoring documentation.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: `timechart span=1h max(poe_w) by port switch_name` has two split-by fields; timechart supports only one (see https://docs.splunk.com/Documentation/Splunk/latest/SearchReference/Timechart). Combine switch_name and port into one field first.
A single 25 W threshold is close to the 802.3at power available to a powered device and far above 802.3af class limits; it is not tied to camera power classes.

summary: The SPL uses two timechart split-by fields, which is not supported, applies one 25 W threshold although the text refers to class budgets, and takes switch PoE data from an NVR diagnostic sourcetype.
